From the vector addition and scalar multiplication rules, we have

$$
{\int }_{0}^{3}[\frac{1}{2}f(t)-g(t)]\,\text{d}t=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t-{\int }_{0}^{3}g(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}[\frac{1}{2}f(t)-g(t)]\,\text{d}t & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t-{\int }_{0}^{3}g(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨-6,\,-2,\,8⟩-⟨4,\,3,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,\,-1,\,4⟩-⟨4,\,3,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨-7,\,-4,\,5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
